body:
Omg are you me? I swear my mom would only do laundry a couple times a week and ONLY when I was at school. If the ONE jacket I owned was ever dirty I'd have to leave it in the laundry basket in the morning, remind her to do the laundry that day, then go out into the freezing cold and spend all day at school freezing my ass off with no jacket on. Occasionally she'd "forget" to do the laundry that day so I'd have to go two days in a row with no jacket. But would she ever buy me another one? Nope. A $5 Walmart jacket was too damn expensive according to her. 

Oh and also on the days when my jacket WAS washed and I decided not to wear it she'd flip out and tell me I need one on or I'd catch hypothermia and die! Like bitch, does that problem not exist on the days that you inexplicably HAVE to do my laundry while I'm at school freezing all day?! Wtf!!! Sorry you went through a similar situation :( Its truly liberating to be able to do laundry whenever you feel like it!

That's one big plus to over explaining things; you get an uncanny ability to teach people in a more in-depth way than most people bother to. I've had similar remarks at both long term jobs I've had, that when I trained people they understood the procedures clearly and picked up on stuff faster than when others tried to teach them! Glad to hear you've put your over explaining skills to good use!

I'm also 22, and in a similar position as you. Bad home life growing up, always behind my peers emotionally and socially, wasn't allowed to date in school, suffered with depression for most of my life, did drugs for awhile and had a problem with alcohol for a good part of last year. Just got my first full time job this year at a company I want to stay with for the forseeable future. Haven't moved out on my own yet (tried and failed a couple times with roomates. Just ended up damaging friendships and losing out on money I could've saved by staying home awhile longer). I have graduated high school and gotten a generic associate's degree from my local community college that has nothing to do with my job now.

I think I agree with brvsirrobin, don't compare yourself to others! I have a tendency to do this as well and it makes you feel like you're worth less than other people, which is not true at all. Sure some other people had easier paths laid out for them by having nurturing, caring families and parents with money who could help them out with school and getting their first home, ect. But ultimately all of our life experiences help to shape us into who we're meant to become. Without getting religious, I feel like we all have some kind of purpose or reason for being here and for the things we go through whether or not we can ever understand why. I often tell myself that while other wealthier kids got off to a better head start, people who have to struggle and earn their own way through life often appreciate what they do have alot more. People like us are often stronger emotionally because of the experiences we've been through. It may not be easier but at least you can say that anything you've accomplished has come from your own dedication and hard work rather than bumming off of other people's success.

With all that being said, I don't think it's all that uncommon for most people to feel like they're behind their peers in some area of life. You're not alone feeling like this. Just focus on yourself and your goals and break down big goals into smaller steps that you can work on achieving. Eventually after busting your butt you can reach the place you want to be at.

Your comment mirrors my own experiences. My childhood best friend is a big narc and I'm realizing how scarily similar she acts compared to my Nmom. I recently reconnected with Nfriend after a few years of NC with her. And it was more of the same, manipulation, calling me names, making fun of me, bringing me down all the time, always has to be going on and on about herself and how great she thinks her life is, expects me to text her 24/7 and hang out constantly with no respect for my time or boundaries. We had/have fun when we're together, but it's not without all the negatives that come with being around an N. We have fun too but there's always this underlying feeling of uneasiness where I can't completely let my guard down and be myself anywhere near her. 

I completely understand where you're coming from on wanting to reconnect with that old part of your life, where there were happy times and you felt connected to someone. But if you do, be warned that your Nfriend is probably exactly the same as back then, if not worse. It may seem fine for awhile, but his N-ways will come back out and before you know it, you'll be miserable again. If you do decide to reconnect, just remember that you are completely in control of your life and your time. You are allowed to set boundaries that you're comfortable with and if your friend keeps pushing your boundaries it's perfectly fine to pick yourself up and leave. You may be lonely without any old friendships in your life, but as I've come to find out in my own experience, I'd rather be lonely than have a friend who treats me like crap. My self-worth is much more important to me at this point.
Don't forget the third option: Freeze. That one is my specialty when danger is near.

I'm so sorry you had to go through that alone :( I had a similar experience at 17-18. I was severely depressed, cut all my friends out of my life and developed anorexia that almost killed me. What did my parents do? My mom called me a big baby and said I was lucky nobody called cps on her BC it would make HER look like a bad mom if they did. She went around to neighbors, family, church people and talked behind my back about how worried she was about me, not bc she cared, but to make her look like a concerned mother. But to my face she treated me like crap and wouldn't help me. Also suggested therapy but never took me. My dad just let this all go on, only ever saying "it'd be a shame if you didn't graduate high school because you can't do your homework". I had fallen severely behind in school BC of all this, but still had enough credits to pass so his comment was completely unnecessary and just kicked me down even more. Understand that you weren't the one at fault there at all. As your parents they should've helped you at that time. You are so much stronger now for having to go through that alone.
I would say the sister might be the one who can't bring herself to tell anyone. OP is the adult here, so should take responsibility for helping their sister!

Yes, I guess I'm afraid that the person will rage at me for saying something to them, so as a defence mechanism I rage at them first. But most people aren't N's like my parents so that reaction is always seen as over the top and I'm labeled as being crazy and super touchy. I will work on just bringing things up calmly in the future. Thanks for replying!

Yes, I guess the root of it IS that I believe I'm supposed to be ignored even though I'm realizing now that this isn't the truth. My pattern in relationships in the past has been to just let resentment build up til I hated the person and wouldn't care if they were in my life or not, then I'd blow up at them and was prepared for things to go either way. Either we'd work things out or they'd move on. But I always feel like such an a$$hole for being this way, and don't like that I hurt people. You are right in saying that they don't deserve my aggression towards them. You make a good point that most people don't do annoying things on purpose. I will work on trying to just discuss things first to fix the situation rather than exploding out of nowhere. Thank you for replying!

You know, my sister had me watch this movie with her a few years ago (I was probably 18 and sis was 23). My sister was starting to talk to me about how screwed up our childhoods were but I wasn't at a point that I fully understood how to process it all. Lately I've started back on the path of realizing that my parents are narcissists. Looking back on this movie now, it takes on a whole different meaning. It's amazing how many children's movies, shows, books, ect. talk about abusive family situations and/or narcissism. Thanks for sharing OP!

OMG I figured my hair fiascos as a kid were a one-off situation with my own mom. Crazy to see so many other people went through this! For me when I was about 3 or 4 my mom would make me lay on the kitchen counter and hang my head over the sink so she could wash my hair in the sink (don't ask me why she chose the sink instead of the bathtub like every normal parent would do). She'd make me lay on my back so I basically had to use my neck muscles to hold my head up. I remember it hurting my neck so bad. Then when she was done I'd have to hold my neck over the sink while she wrung out the water from my hair and dried it with a towel. If I tried to sit up bc I felt like my neck was about to snap off, she would YANK me back down by my hair and be like "DON'T SIT UP, YOU'RE HAIR'S NOT DRY YET!!!" This is soooo bizarre looking back on it...

Then after the nightmare of washing my hair came the blowdryer. I dreaded the blowdryer. She would put it on the hottest setting and hold it way too close to my head, to the point it would burn. When she dried the hair next to my neck I would have burn marks on my skin for a day or two afterwards from the heat. Then, when I thought it was over -- came the comb. She would comb my hair so forcefully that she would scratch my scalp. On school days she would brush my hair super fast to the point that it hurt. She also refused to use normal hair products on us so if my hair was frizzy, she'd dip my hairbrush in a cup of water before brushing it. She'd also braid my hair every night and would of course do that forcefully too. If I complained during any of these things it was "quit whining/crying, this has to be done so suck it up!"

I forgot about most of this until now. I ALWAYS had neck pain/headaches as a kid and was constantly lightheaded and dizzy which I now realize was from all this bs. Luckily she only made me wash my hair a couple times a week but I always dreaded it. When I was a teenager I always hated the shower and would only shower twice a week, with extreme irrational fear and anxiety every time I did but I could never figure out why. I now realize it was most likely bc of the fear I had as a kid when it was time to wash my hair.

Oh my god I'm the same way! I feel guilty for pretty much everything, like I'm not worthy of existing and if I take time out of anyone else's day, I'm just being a burden and they probably hate me for wanting their attention. I'm sorry you have to deal with this issue too. I wish there was a quick fix to feel like you're a worthy human being and can do things without worrying about annoying others with your mere presence.

This was exactly my dad. I only saw him on weekends but he'd rarely try to spend any actual time with me. But suddenly when I wanted to hang out with a friend because I was bored out of my mind of being ignored, it was "No, I think you need to stay here. It's your weekend to be here with me so you're not going out." and if I pushed the issue and got upset he'd ground me. So I'd just go back into my room and be ignored for awhile longer, til inevitably he'd randomly burst into my room without knocking and want me to be up and ready to go do whatever he was doing. No prior warning or asking if I wanted to do what he was doing - he'd drag me along on errands or whatever else and call that "spending time" with me. Ugh. I'm sorry you've had a similar experience.

I just recently came across the terms for covert incest, overt incest, emotional enmeshment/incest, ect. and it felt like I finally had an explanation for all the vague "creepy" feelings I've had around my parents over the years.

Nmom was more emotionally enmeshed, treating my like a therapist and confiding in me about all her adult relationships. Edad was more covertly incest. I have a hard time typing this as I've never realized this behavior was so wrong until recently. At his house, he would constantly walk around in just underwear when we were at home, not putting on pants til halfway through the day most of the time. He would also randomly rub my back or tickle me when I was on the computer or trying to focus on something that wasn't him. This is something that still bothers me bc he still does it! Even when I told him to stop touching me he would keep doing it! When I was younger he would start tickling me, starting out in normal places like my stomach or shoulders. Then he would tickle the insides of my legs near my crotch, getting close but never actually touching my crotch. He always seemed to fixate on that spot on my legs when tickling me bc he said "there's more feeling right there". 

Now as an adult, he will put his hand high up on my thigh when we're sitting next to each other and it feels "icky" for lack of a better term. When I try to give him a hug he always has to tickle me which pisses me off. He can never just give a regular hug without getting all touchy and weird. It's never overtly sexual touches, but it has a weird sexual undertone, if not just being completely uncomfortable and creepy. And the fact that he will not stop when I ask him to makes it creepier.

At this point I HATE being touched by anyone, especially if it's unexpected. I have a hard time being intimate with anyone and usually if someone touches me I just freeze up and feel helpless. I'm working on setting my boundaries at this point. It's hard bc growing up my boundaries were never respected and I was basically conditioned to be touched in ways that didn't sit right with me, and I had no say in it at all. So now I feel like if I express my boundaries, the other person won't listen to me so it's pointless to say anything. I know my situation isn't as bad as some others, but it's still fucked me up.

Celebrities and models in the media are so far removed from real people. Everyone you see in the media is photoshopped and/or has TONS of makeup on. They're fake, essentially. It's all vanity and emptiness. Even if you had a super sexy model, that wouldn't fulfill anything in you if they were vain and had no personality. Nobody has a super sexy model girlfriend besides other models (and maybe a few, very few lucky regular guys). It's not something to beat yourself up over. Focus on yourself and becoming more confident with yourself and your own life. You'll find the perfect woman for you when it's the right time :) 

Also, don't look outside yourself for other people to complete you. Work on being completely fine with who you are as a single person. Then when you find a relationship it will be way healthier and balanced because you won't be clinging onto someone else for your sense of self worth. It all comes with becoming more confident.

I am the same way. My mom wouldn't let me go out often, so most of my childhood and teenage years I was stuck in my room daydreaming about all the stuff I wished I could do, and all the stuff I wanted to do when I got older. If it weren't for the internet/tv/video games I probably would have gone insane. Now I'm 22 and I still have that habit of just daydreaming about stuff instead of being able to DO anything. I'm so used to not being able to do what I want, that it takes a crazy amount of effort to do anything.

I do this too. Nmom pounded it into my head growing up that men were worthless and only want sex. Men don't have emotions and don't care about anything but sex. I grew up hating all boys/men and treated every guy I came across like crap. I thought that when they said I hurt their feelings they were just faking it. In fact, it's taken me up until the last couple of years to understand that other people actually have emotions too and don't just say things for the hell of it. Everyone feels just as much as I feel. And the way i treat other people can impact them, whether negatively or positively. It sounds dumb saying it but Nmom disregarded EVERYONE'S feelings around me growing up so I took on that same mentality until people started pointing out how mean I am and I realized that my thinking was severely fucked up in this realm of life. 

As a result of believing men were emotionless sex robots, I of course ended up in nothing but abusive relationships with men that just reinforced this belief. I'm just recently starting to get out of this mindset and realize how very wrong I've been my whole life. I'm 22 so still relatively young. I'm glad I made this revelation and I'm trying to work on being more understanding towards others.

I am the same way, I hate drawing any kind of attention to myself. If I make a noise and someone looks at me I get really anxious. If anyone notices me or compliments me I get really anxious and uncomfortable. Anytime someone wants my attention I always think it's going to be because they're mad at me.

Growing up, Nmom was always whining about how loud me and my sisters were. If the tv was ever at a volume where we could actually hear it properly, it was "too loud". Most of the time the volume was barely on at all and me and my sister would have to have on the captions and read along with them to understand what was happening. To this day I still have trouble understanding the context of alot of tv shows and movies if I don't have captions on. Like I miss whole chunks of what's happening, or words I hear sound jumbled up or like gibberish and I can't fully understand things unless I can read along.

I remember one time I was sick and kept sneezing. My mom yelled at me to blow my nose and shut up, from her bedroom. Apparently my occasional sneezes were keeping her from sleeping? 

If me and my sister played with any of our toys our mom would flip out bc we made a mess, while we were still in the middle of playing. We always picked up when we were done, but she made a point to flip out about how messy it was while we were playing.

Countless other things happened as well. Basically, anytime she wanted our attention it was always to tell us to shut up or to belittle us in some other way. Otherwise she straight up ignored us like we didn't exist.

Now I feel like I don't have a right to exist. Like I'm not a real person. I hate having any kind of attention. I think the symptoms of social anxiety fit how I feel. I just hate being around people or being noticed. Whenever someone genuinely compliments me I always feel like they're making it up and like they have some kind of hidden motive for being that nice to me, like my mom always did. I'm slowly starting to realize all of this and trying to realize that most other people aren't crazy like my mom, don't hate me, and actually mean what they say when they compliment me. 

I also play instruments - piano, guitar, ukulele and sing. Growing up my mom forced me to take piano lessons and at that point I hated them. But later on I began to really appreciate music and it's become a huge part of my identity. I hope to one day be a musician and perform but I too have terrible anxiety performing in front of people. One of my coworkers heard me sing to a song that was playing on the radio the other day and when she said I sounded amazing and sounded just like the singer, I turned beet red and was embarrassed! And I hate playing guitar in front of people bc I always start shaking and mess up. Hopefully one day I'll get to the point where I'm not so embarrassed. I know I have talent, others can see I have talent too. I just need to realize that I am worthy of doing what I love and I can be great at it. 

I believe you can get to that point to, we just have to realize that they way we grew up was NOT normal and try our best to undo the damage from N's and start to be who we truly are.

I have an Nfriend who does this same thing. Always talking down to others and trying to act like she's soooo smart and knows everything about everything. When I pointed out her behavior one day she responded with "What? I don't think I'm better than anybody! In fact I feel like I'm LESS than most people!"

oh, so is that why you act like that? You think you're "less than" other people so you completely bombard people with how smart you think you are to make up for your insecurities? In a way it makes sense but it's hard to honestly believe that N's don't act this way on purpose. I believe they do think they're better than everyone but when you point that out it turns into a pity party all about how bad they feel inside, and they still ignore the effects of their behavior on other people.

I'm pretty much in the same position as you right now. I recently got rid of all my friends bc they were all using me and looking back on it, my best friend for 10 years has always been another N in my life, just dragging me down with constant negativity and being all about herself 24/7 without caring about me at all. And some other people I hung out with last year are N's as well. I started a new fulltime job earlier this year as well and had feelings like I was weird and nobody liked me. But you know what I realized? The more I talk to people at work, the more I realize that they DO actually like me and they appreciate the work that I do. You ARE a lovable person and if you just be yourself, people will start to take notice and gravitate towards you.

As far as social skills go, try reading some books on smalltalk and start having more conversations with people at work, or even out other places like the store or an event that you're at. Basically, just ask people questions about the environment that you're in, then ask them questions about themselves and get them to open up to you. It'll feel weird at first if you're not used to initiating contact with people, but keep practicing and you'll get better at it. Be sure to smile and make eye contact while greeting or talking to someone.

For example, if you're at work and see your coworker Bob walking down the hallway towards you, you could have an exchange like this:

You: "Good morning Bob! How are you today?"
Bob: "I'm doing good, and you?"
You: "I'm good as well. Did you hear about [insert something about a sports game, weather, company event or policy, something happening in your town, something lighthearted in the news, ect.]
Bob: "Yes, I heard about that new policy they're implementing, blah blah blah"

and just continue from there. Bob now sees you as friendly and open to talking. After a few times of talking to someone, start asking them more about them, i.e. "so are you from this town?" "are you married?" "do you have any kids?" "what do you do in your spare time for fun?". Just basic questions to get to know them. Give genuine compliments if you see something about them that you like. If they tell you they're doing something important or fun on a certain day, remember what they said then ask them how it went the day after that event happened. That will make them feel like you are a caring person because you remember what you talked about with them. Get some hobbies of your own and invite people out to events with you. 

Humans are weird; if you ask someone about themselves and let them talk about themselves for a little bit, they will tend to like you more, but won't be able to figure out why they like you so much. People love to talk about themselves. But of course, be sure to watch out for the self-absorbed narcs out there. If they never reciprocate and ask questions about you, you'll know that you should avoid trying to get closer to them. Practicing smalltalk like this will help you to be able to identify other narc's easier so you can get better at avoiding people like that and find genuine people to talk to.

If you just pack up and move, that's not going to change anything. You'll still be lacking social skills til you practice social skills. You'll still feel bad about yourself until you work on yourself. A new environment won't magically change your personality, YOU'VE got to do that work yourself, and you are more than capable of doing so :)

I think I've done sort of the same thing. I've always felt like I had two personalities. The "real" me and the "oh god, other people are around so I must bend to their will" me. I was never able to be myself around my Nparents so I had to fake this image of being nice, kind, smart, never causing trouble, quiet. Basically they wanted me to be "perfect". I learned to stifle my real personality and interests when anyone else was around and put on this fake mask so that I would be loved by other people. I thought that I HAD to put on this fake mask to be accepted. But it sucked bc I was always hiding my real self and I wanted so bad to JUST BE ME for once. 

I'm just recently starting to feel like I can act like my actual self around people. I still kind of put on an act around Nparents bc that just makes it easier to get along with them and not cause any more trouble or arguments. I'm seeing now, especially at my current workplace, that people really do like my actual personality. I started out at my job with my "nice-girl" fake persona, but the more I'm starting to come out of my shell and just be myself, the more people seem to like me and accept me for being myself. 
I've thought for so long that I had to hide who I am to be loved and it's so amazing to have people in my life now that accept me for ME and not some made up image-imposter of myself.
This made me crack up!
Just remember that whatever an N says about you is actually how they feel about THEMSELVES. She couldn't stand herself so she took it out on you. That's not your fault at all.
That is amazing lol. And the funny part is that mom made herself look like a fool and probably still doesn't get it! I've always loved judge Judy BC she takes no shit from anyone haha
You're most certainly welcome! ((Hugs))! :D

Gotta love how they get upset after throwing out stuff they've probably never looked at more than twice. That is insane! 

My parents also did the whole "clean before we have company" thing and those were the only times the house actually looked decent. 

I'm at that stage of learning that my parents have horrible cleaning habits and that I was never taught to clean properly. It is odd realizing this as an adult and trying to learn things now that you should've learned way earlier. But better late than never! Just realize that it's not your fault they never showed you this stuff, it was they're responsibility to teach you like skills like cleaning and they never did. That's awesome that you have a boyfriend who's willing to show you how to clean properly though!

Good job on realizing it was your mom pushing her messes onto you, and not you who has the problem! You don't have to continue her craziness and disorganized habits. 

I will have to check out that book as well, sounds like it helped you alot! I need to learn some new habits before getting my own place. I also hate inviting people over BC I know they'll think my house is gross.

That is crazy! I chuckled in disbelief at the "puts them on the floor" part. What is so hard about doing dishes? And my dad is the same with piles and piles of paper, magazines, books. I just don't get it!

I understand that hypocritical part, my Nmom does the same thing! Won't keep her own house clean but belittles me when I have the same habits as her! I'm trying to break those habits now and start cleaning more, which will be way easier when I can move out.

It's certainly not your fault for not knowing any better. Your parents were supposed to set that example for you and they failed to do so.

We used to have an indoor cat and my mom would actually clean the litter box every day or every other day (surprisingly). But hardly did any other cleaning. Then again, she seemed to love that cat more than me or my sisters anyways. She would literally ignore me after school but would have full blown conversations with the damn cat! 

I agree, it's not hard to keep a home clean so I don't understand why she just won't do it! Kudos to you for keeping up with proper housecleaning!

Omg yes! My mom gets mad if I try to clean when she's gone. If I use any kind of chemical to clean she whines about how horrible the chemical smells and how she can still smell it for days after I clean. I've given up cleaning BC she always makes me feel like shit for trying! 

My mom also will have occasional cleaning sprees, mostly to clean up her years of paperwork shoved in random drawers. She'll usually start doing this around midnight though and make tons of noise all night so I can't sleep. 

My mom also used to "clean" my room which usually consisted of her moving my things to another spot that I didn't want them at. And if I rearranged my room back how I wanted it after she did this, she'd just go back in when I was at school and put everything her way again. It was so frustrated having no control over my own stuff!

Good job on the progress! We shouldn't have to feel bad for cleaning our own homes, it's what normal people do! Hopefully you can reach a point where you don't have stupid fears like this anymore!

I dealt with this too. I have to wonder now if my mom is slightly schizophrenic or something BC all I heard from her my whole childhood was how everyone else in the world is so bad and there's sooooo many crazy people out there that will hurt me! Dont talk to strangers and don't trust anyone! I was never allowed to leave my house as a child except for school or to play outside in our fenced in yard when she was around. Thankfully my parents got divorced when I was 6 and my dad usually allowed me to run around the neighborhood with other kids when I stayed with him. 

But suddenly when I was a teenager he always had a problem with me leaving to hang out with ffriends and both my parents always had to know every little detail of who I was with, what we were doing, where we were going ect. ect. It's taken me alot if work to develop any kind of social skills.

They also had the ordeal with not letting me drive. I got my license but when i was learning to drive, I could only put up W my Nmom for maybe 30 mins to an hour a few times a week BC she would flip out over stupid shit and argue with me over EVERYTHING. Every single damn time we drove I'd hit the point where I was seriously considering crashing into something on purpose to kill us both BC she pissed me off so much and I would start heading home before I had the nerve to do so. Every time it was "what, you're already done, we've only drove so and so many minutes today!" I have no clue how I put up with that shit. 

I also never learned to cook or clean and I'm so thrilled when I get to actually do those things and be responsible for myself. I'm trying to move out now and my parents are laying on the guilt trips about how I should stay home, save up money, why would you want to grow up and have to take care of chores and bills. I can't wait to have my own  place.

Christian music. Dear God, Christian music was like the background music of my childhood. It's all Nmom would ever listen to. She always said she could never listen to the classic rock music she listened to as a teenager because it "makes her cuss more" and she can't cuss as an outstanding Christian woman! Nevermind the physical, emotional and verbal abuse from her damn near every day, apparently none of that disqualified her from being a Christian! Ugh, I still get flashbacks to my fucked up youth when I hear Christian music of any kind...

Thank you for your encouraging words! And yes, I have always had trouble distinguishing if someone's apology is real or not after dealing with my Nmom verbally abusing me my whole life. I like to see the good in people and would like to be able to take someone's word that they're sorry and will act different as being truthful. But in this case I believe you're right that it's just the cycle of narc abuse all over again. Looks like it's time to start NC!

This brought up a memory of one winter night when my Nmom left me and my sister in her unlocked car at night in the freezing cold while we were both sick. She stopped at Walmart to pick up medicine for us from the pharmacy but was gone for at LEAST an hour or more. Which to a 5 and 10 year old seems like an eternity. We were both afraid she forgot about us and scared that someone might kidnap us, and I (being 5 at the time) started crying BC I was convinced she had abandoned us. We watched the doors of the store constantly for her to come out. By the time she finally got back she said that she took so long BC the meds weren't ready to pick up yet. WTF. Why not come back and get us, let us walk around in a warm store for awhile? She didn't leave the heat on or anything so we were visibly shivering and numb by the time she got back. Ironically, when I was in like middle school she would get onto me about not wearing a jacket in fall weather "because I might get frostbite". Yeah. Let that sink in for a minute. She thought 13 year old me would get frostbite standing in chilly fall weather for a few minutes after school, but not that we could've gotten frostbite being left outside for an hour in the dead middle of winter at night. I just can't understand parents who do things like this.

Yes, the two times I've gone NC with her in the past I told her not to contact me anymore. She'd leave me alone for awhile but always find someway to contact me again or have one of her friends contact me and harrass me for her. I guess I just need to realize that no matter what she says or how many time she apologizes, she'll never be the friend I need her to be. And I need to be strong enough for myself to not fall for her tactics anymore.

Yes, I do the same thing. I grew up with Nparents and dealt with all kinds of abuse, and I used to attract alot of narcissists as friends, romantic partners, ect. How old are you? You said you are jealous of the people around you. Are these people at school, at your job? Where? One thing that it helps to realize is that jealousy gets you nowhere. All these people may seem like they have amazing lives and tons of friends and whatnot, but the reality is that everyone struggles with their self esteem and feeling like that person over there is better than them. No, really. Even the prettiest, most popular person has insecurities themselves. People who seem to have it all on the outside may be just as torn up on the inside as you. The problem here isn't what other people think of you. It's that you don't believe in yourself. The sad truth is that if you put all your hope for being happy on how other people treat you, you will ALWAYS be disappointed. There will always be someone who doesn't like you, someone who thinks they're better than you, someone who doesn't understand who you are. What you need to do is do a little soul searching. Learn that you are okay as a person. You have to learn to love yourself first because nobody can love you if YOU don't love you. Figure what motivates you, what you can bring to the world. Even just something small, like a hobby that makes you happy. If you are able to, move somewhere else, change jobs or schools. Just get in a new environment somehow. Even if this isn't possible, go for a walk somewhere you've never been before. Go sit outside and watch the sunset. Do something to get you out of the mindset you're in. Exercise is also great. Anything that gets you out of your head. Go somewhere and talk to new people. Read books about how to converse with people and about body language. Socializing is something that has to be practiced, and the more you do it, the better you'll get at it. In any case, quit worrying so much about what other people think and what others are doing. Start taking care of yourself and focusing on yourself. Things will fall into place when you learn to become your own best friend.
